title: FDA Appendix F: the narrow therapeutic index procedure, three criteria
subject: narrow therapeutic index drugs

rule.statement: For an NTI drug on a fully replicate crossover design, T is bioequivalent to R for a PK parameter only when ALL THREE of the following hold: (a) the 95% upper confidence bound for (mu_T - mu_R)^2 - theta*sigma_WR^2 is <= 0; (b) the regular unscaled BE limits of 80.00%-125.00% are passed; (c) the upper limit of the 90% equal-tails confidence interval for sigma_WT / sigma_WR is <= 2.500.
rule.not_a_narrowed_interval: FDA NTI is not ordinary average BE on a narrowed acceptance range. There is no 90.00-111.11% in this procedure at all.

design_gate.statement: For NTI drugs, a fully replicate crossover design should be used.
design_gate.why_it_is_a_gate: The procedure has three criteria, one of which compares within-subject test and reference variability and therefore needs TWO test measurements per subject. A partial replicate gives one. Falling back to ordinary average BE would replace a three-criterion procedure with a one-criterion one.

reference_variance.m_note: Appendix F step 1: 'm = 2 for fully replicate design: TRTR and RTRT'. The same closed form Appendix G gives, restricted to the fully replicate case.
reference_variance.citation_note: The implementation is shared with the highly variable procedure. The CITATION is not: an NTI decision rests on Appendix F step 1, and the result must not cite Appendix G.

test_variance.formula: sWT^2 = SUM_i SUM_j (DTij - DTbar_i.)^2 / (2(n - m)), with DTij = Tij1 - Tij2
test_variance.interpretation_note: Appendix F step 1 gives the closed form for sWR ONLY. Step 4 names sWT - 'the estimate of sigma_WT with v1 as the degree of freedom' - without restating how to compute it. What is implemented is the same estimator applied to the subject's two TEST observations: the symmetric reading, and what Appendix C's REPEATED/GRP=TRT SUB=SUBJ residual structure produces. Recorded as an interpretation, not as transcription.

delta_precision_discrepancy.classification: precision discrepancy between the stated constant and the example-code approximation
delta_precision_discrepancy.not_a_contradiction: This is NOT the guidance contradicting itself and it does not affect the algorithm, which is identical either way. Appendix F's prose states the constant and offers its own five-decimal approximation in the same sentence; the SAS example then prints that approximation, which is what example code does. Recording it as a contradiction would misrepresent the document.
delta_precision_discrepancy.why_it_is_still_recorded: Criterion (a) has a boundary, so 'too small to matter' is a claim rather than a fact. A synthetic near-boundary case exists in which the same data pass under the prose constant and fail under the example-code literal - the band is about 4e-08 wide in sWR^2. Neither value is rounded into the other, and the example literal is stored outside FDA_NTI_CONSTANTS so it can never be iterated as a regulatory constant.
delta_precision_discrepancy.compare_with_the_highly_variable_case: There the regulator's stated value WAS the rounded one (sWR = 0.294, not the derived 0.293560). The two point opposite ways, which is why each constant is decided from its own text rather than from a general preference for exact arithmetic.

howe_comparison.claim: Appendix F step 2 and Appendix G step 2 use an identical construction, differing only in theta.
howe_comparison.consequence: one shared helper taking theta as an argument, with a wrapper per procedure supplying its own constants and its own citation. NOT a generic routine with a mode flag.

a.statement: The 95% upper confidence bound for (mu_T - mu_R)^2 - theta*sigma_WR^2 must be <= 0

b.statement: Regular unscaled BE limits of 80.00%-125.00% should be passed.
b.not_the_ema_interval: 90.00-111.11% is EMA's narrowed interval for the same drug class. FDA does not narrow - it adds criteria. Using the narrowed limits here would be the single most consequential substitution available in this procedure.
b.why_not: the unscaled average BE analysis of a fully replicate study is FDA Appendix C's mixed model, which is not implemented. Appendix F's own ilat interval is a different model - no period term, one residual variance, no subject-by-formulation covariance - and is not substituted.
b.expected_note: the containment test is written out and tested so that implementing Appendix C is a matter of supplying the interval, not of also deciding what to do with it. It is not exercised by the pipeline in this release.

c.statement: The upper limit of the 90% equal-tails confidence interval for sigma_WT / sigma_WR must be less than or equal to 2.500
c.tail_convention: F_p(v1, v2) is the value with probability p to its RIGHT - an upper-tail quantile, scipy.stats.f.isf(p, v1, v2), NOT f.ppf. The wrong tail gives an interval that is still ordered and still positive.
c.degrees_of_freedom: v1 belongs to sWT, v2 to sWR. They differ whenever a subject is missing one of its four measurements.

conjunction.statement: For T to be bioequivalent to R, the following conditions must be satisfied for each PK parameter tested
conjunction.missing_is_not_failure: a criterion that was not computed yields None, and the overall decision is NOT DECIDED. An endpoint never tested against the unscaled limits is untested under this procedure - neither bioequivalent nor inequivalent.

zero_reference_sd.situation: sWR = 0 is a legitimate variance estimate and is reported as one; criterion c divides by it.
zero_reference_sd.handling: the ratio is undefined. Not infinity, not 'very large therefore fails'. The criterion is unavailable, a REFERENCE_SD_ZERO_VARIANCE_RATIO_UNDEFINED diagnostic is raised, and the endpoint is NOT DECIDED.

endpoint_scope.statement: Appendix F step 1 determines sWR 'for the PK parameters including AUC and Cmax', and step 5 applies the conditions 'for each PK parameter tested'.
endpoint_scope.consequence: AUC and Cmax are assessed independently; one endpoint's outcome must not enter the other's arithmetic.

source.section: III.B and Appendix F (steps 1-5 and the SAS example)
source.verified_by: primary document, read at the cited section
source.limitation: The guidance states the algorithm, the constants and the SAS route for steps 1-2, and contains no worked dataset - no input values and no published answer anywhere in the document. So this closes tier 1A for the criteria and cannot close tier 1B. No external numerical oracle has been run either: PowerTOST would be a tier-3 cross-check and R is not available in this environment. Separately, sWT is an interpretation rather than a transcription - Appendix F states the closed form for sWR only.

covers: The design gate, the two computable criteria, the conjunction of all three, the constants and their discrepancy, and the zero-reference handling. It asserts nothing about EMA ABEL, which is not implemented, and nothing about Appendix C, which criterion b needs.
